##### **UC08 \- Sync Data from FAP (simulator)**

| Primary Actor(s): | Academic Staff | Secondary Actor(s): | FPT Academic Portal (FAP) |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Description:** | Allows an academic staff member to trigger a full data synchronization from the FPT Academic Portal (FAP) to import or update academic data including students, groups, topics, classes, semesters, and lecturers into the system. |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | The Staff is authenticated and has an active session. The system has a valid and configured connection to FAP. FAP is available and accessible at the time of synchronization. |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | All relevant academic data including students, groups, topics, classes, semesters, and lecturers are successfully updated in the system. The system reflects the latest data retrieved from FAP after synchronization. If synchronization fails, the existing data in the system remains unchanged. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | NF-01: The Staff is on the Academic Staff Home Page → clicks the Sync Data From FAP button under the Quick Actions section. NF-02: The system displays the Sync Academic Data dialog containing a brief instruction, a Previous Course dropdown, and a Next Course dropdown. NF-03: The Staff selects the desired course code from the Previous Course dropdown → selects the desired course code from the Next Course dropdown → clicks the Sync button. NF-04: The system sends a data request to the FAP API using the selected course codes → compares the received data with existing records to determine which records need to be inserted or updated → imports new records and updates existing records accordingly → completes the synchronization process and closes the dialog. → displays a sync success notification. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flow:** |  |  |  |
| **Extension Flow:** | ETF-01: At NF-03, if the Staff clicks the X button or clicks outside the dialog, the system closes the dialog and no synchronization is performed. ETF-02: At NF-03, if the Staff clicks the Cancel button, the system closes the dialog and no synchronization is performed. |  |  |
| **Exceptions Flow:** | EF-01: At NF-04, if the Staff selects the same course code for both Previous Course and Next Course, the system displays a validation message indicating that the two courses must not be at the same level and prevents synchronization. EF-01: At NF-04, if the selected Previous Course and Next Course are not exactly one level apart, the system displays a validation message indicating that the two courses must be consecutive levels and prevents synchronization. EF-01: At NF-04, if the selected Previous Course is at a higher level than the Next Course, the system displays a validation message indicating that the Previous Course must be one level lower than the Next Course and prevents synchronization. |  |  |
| **Business Rule** | BR-01: Only users with the Staff role or higher may trigger a data synchronization from FAP. BR-02: Both Previous Course and Next Course must be selected before the synchronization can be initiated. |  |  |

##### **UC13 \- Manage Course**

| Primary Actor(s): | Academic Staff | Secondary Actor(s): |  |
| :---- | ----- | :---- | :---- |
| **Description:** | Allows a staff member to manage courses within their assigned campus. The staff can view the list of courses, create new courses, update existing course information, and delete courses when necessary. |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | The Staff is authenticated and has an active session. The Staff has been assigned to a specific campus in the system. |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | **View**: The system displays the course list accurately based on the latest data within the Staff's campus scope. **Create**: A new course is created and available in the system. **Update**: The selected course reflects the latest updated information. **Delete**: The selected course is removed from the system. If any operation fails, the system data remains unchanged. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | **View Course List** NF-01: The Staff navigates to the Course Management section by selecting “Manage Course” in the staff home page. NF-02: The system retrieves and displays the list of all courses belonging to the Staff's assigned campus, including relevant information such as course code, course name, level, credits, status, and grade items table. **Create Course** NF-03: The Staff selects the “Add Course” option  to create a new course. NF-04: The system displays a form for entering new course information. NF-05: The Staff fills in the required fields including course code, course name, credits, course level, status, and description (optional). NF-06: The Staff selects the “Create Course” to submit the form. NF-07: The system validates and creates the new course. NF-08: The system displays a success notification and redirects the latest course list. **Update Course** NF-03: The Staff selects a course from the list and chooses the edit option. NF-04: The system displays the selected course's current information in an editable form. NF-05: The Staff modifies the desired fields. NF-06: The Staff selects “Update Course" to submit the updated information. NF-07: The system validates the submitted data and saves the updated information. NF-08: The system displays a success notification and reflects the updated information in the course list. **Delete Course** NF-03: The Staff selects a course from the list and chooses the delete option. NF-04: The system displays a confirmation dialog asking the Staff to confirm the deletion. NF-05: The Staff confirms the deletion. NF-06: The system removes the selected course. NF-07: The system displays a success notification and updates the course list accordingly. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flow:** | AF-01: At NF-02, the staff selects a course from the list and chooses the view option. The system displays course detail information. The staff selects the “Edit” option to update the course. Continue NF-04 **(Update Course)** to end **Update Course** flow. |  |  |
| **Extension Flow:** | ETF-01: At NF-04 **(Create Course)**, if the Staff decides not to proceed, the Staff selects cancel and the system discards all input and returns to the course list. ETF-02:  At NF-04 **(Update Course)**, if the Staff decides not to save changes, the Staff selects cancel and the system discards all changes and returns to the course list. ETF-03: At NF-04 **(Delete Course)**, if the Staff cancels the confirmation dialog, the system dismisses the dialog and no deletion is performed. |  |  |
| **Exceptions Flow:** | EF-01: During Create, if the provided course code already exists within the campus, the system displays a duplicate course code error and prevents course creation. EF-02: During Update, if required fields are left empty or submitted data is in an invalid format, the system highlights the invalid fields and displays validation messages without submitting the form. EF-03: During Delete, if the selected course is currently associated with active students, groups, or ongoing academic activities, the system prevents deletion and displays an appropriate warning message. |  |  |
| **Business Rule** | BR-01: A Staff member may only manage courses that belong to their assigned campus; cross-campus course management is not permitted. BR-02: Each course must have a unique course code within the same campus. BR-03: Required fields such as course code, course name, credits and course level must be provided when creating or updating a course. BR-04: A course that is currently linked to active students, groups, or academic activities must not be deleted without resolving those dependencies first. |  |  |

##### **UC14 \- Configure Grade Items**

##### 

| Primary Actor(s): | Academic Staff | Secondary Actor(s): |  |
| :---- | ----- | :---- | :---- |
| **Description:** | Allows a staff member to configure the grading scheme for a specific course by managing grade items. The staff can add new grade items with a defined name and percentage weight, update existing grade items, and delete them when necessary. |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | The Staff is authenticated and has an active session. The Staff has been assigned to a specific campus in the system. The Staff has navigated to the Course Detail page of a specific course. |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | Add: A new grade item is added to the course's grading scheme and stored in the system. Update: The selected grade item reflects the latest updated information. Delete: The selected grade item is removed from the course's grading scheme. If any operation fails, the course's grading configuration remains unchanged. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** |  **Add Grade Item** NF-01: The Staff selects the “Add Grade Item” option to add a new grade item. NF-02: The system displays an input form for entering the grade item name and percentage weight. NF-03: The Staff enters the grade item name and percentage weight. NF-04: The Staff selects the “Create” option to submit the new grade item. NF-05: The system validates the submitted data and saves the new grade item. NF-06: The system updates the grade item list and recalculates the displayed total weight. NF-07: The system displays a success notification. **Update Grade Item** NF-01: The Staff selects an existing grade item and chooses the edit option. NF-02: The system displays the selected grade item's current information in an editable form. NF-03: The Staff modifies the name or percentage weight as needed. NF-04: The Staff selects the “Save” option to submit the updated information. NF-05: The system validates the submitted data and saves the updated grade item NF-06: The system updates the grade item list and recalculates the displayed total weight. NF-07: The system displays a success notification. **Delete Grade Item** NF-01: The Staff selects an existing grade item and chooses the delete option. NF-02: The system displays a confirmation dialog asking the Staff to confirm the deletion. NF-03: The Staff confirms the deletion. NF-04: The system removes the selected grade item. NF-05: The system updates the grade item list and recalculates the displayed total weight. NF-06: The system displays a success notification. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flow:** |  |  |  |
| **Extension Flow:** | ETF-01: At NF-03 **(Add Grade Item/Update Grade Item)**, if the Staff decides not to proceed, the Staff selects the “x” icon and the system discards all input and returns to the grade item list. ETF-02: At NF-02 **(Delete Grade Item),** if the Staff cancels the confirmation dialog, the system dismisses the dialog and no deletion is performed. |  |  |
| **Exceptions Flow:** | EF-01: At NF-04 **(Add Grade Item/Update Grade Item)**, if the new or updated weight causes the total weight of all grade items to exceed 100%, the system displays a validation message indicating the total weight constraint is violated and prevents submission. EF-02: At NF-04 **(Add Grade Item/Update Grade Item)**, if the name field is left empty, the system displays a validation message and prevents submission. |  |  |
| **Business Rule** | BR-01: A Staff member may only configure grade items for courses belonging to their assigned campus. BR-02: Each grade item must have a unique name within the same course. BR-03: The percentage weight of each grade item must be a positive numeric value greater than zero. |  |  |

| **Postconditions:** | View: The system displays the group list and group details accurately based on the latest data. Create: A new group is created and available within the class. Update: The selected group reflects the latest updated member information. Delete: The selected group is removed from the class. If any operation fails, the system data remains unchanged. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | **View Group Detail** NF-01: The Lecturer selects the name of the group from the group list. NF-02: The system retrieves and displays the Group Detail page, including group name, group status, list of members with their student codes, names, and majors, topic, and assigned mentor. **Create Group** NF-01: The Lecturer selects the “Add Group” option to create a new group. NF-02: The system displays a dialog form for entering new group information including unassigned student list dropdown. NF-03: The Lecturer selects unassigned students from the class to add as members → selects “Create Group” to submit the form. NF-04: The system validates the submitted data → creates the new group → displays a success notification, closes create dialog and updates the group list to include the new group. **Update Group** NF-03 (from NF-02 View Group Detail): The Lecturer selects the edit option. NF-04: The system displays the update group dialog within the selected students current information in an editable form. NF-05: The Lecturer adjusts the member list by adding or removing students → submits the updated information. NF-06: The system validates the submitted data →  saves the updated group information →  displays a success notification, closes update dialog and reflects the updated information in the group list. **Delete Group** NF-03 (from NF-02 View Group Detail): The Lecturer selects the delete option. NF-04: The system displays a confirmation dialog asking the Lecturer to confirm the deletion. NF-05: The Lecturer confirms the deletion. NF-06: The system removes the selected group → displays a success notification and redirects to the class detail page. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flow:** |  |  |  |
| **Extension Flow:** | ETF-01: During Create, if the Lecturer decides not to proceed, the Lecturer selects cancel and the system discards all input and closes the create dialog. ETF-02: During Update, if the Lecturer decides not to save changes, the Lecturer selects cancel and the system discards all changes and closes the update dialog. ETF-03: During Delete, if the Lecturer cancels the confirmation dialog, the system dismisses the dialog and no deletion is performed. |  |  |
| **Exceptions Flow:** | EF-01: During Create or Update, if a selected student is greater than max member, the system displays an error and prevents submission. |  |  |
| **Business Rule** | BR-01: The group name is automatically generated by the system. BR-02: A Lecturer may only manage groups within classes that have been explicitly assigned to them. BR-03: Each group must have a unique name within the same class. BR-04: Each group must have at least two members from different majors designated at the time of formation. |  |  |

##### **UC21 \- Publish Group**

| Primary Actor(s): | Lecturer | Secondary Actor(s): |  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Description:** | Allows a lecturer to publish the finalized group list of a class, making it visible to students. Once published, students can view their assigned group within the class.  |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | The Lecturer is authenticated and has an active session. The Lecturer has navigated to the Class Detail page of a specific class. |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | The group list is published and becomes visible to all students within the class. Students can view their assigned group after publication. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | NF-01: The Lecturer reviews the finalized group list → clicks the Publish Group button. NF-02: The system displays a confirmation dialog asking the Lecturer to confirm the publication. NF-03: The Lecturer confirms the action. NF-04: The system makes the group list visible to all students within the class → displays a success notification confirming the group list has been published. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flow:** |  |  |  |
| **Extension Flow:** | ETF-01: At NF-03, if the Lecturer cancels the confirmation dialog, the system dismisses the dialog and no publication is performed. |  |  |
| **Exceptions Flow:** | EF-01: At step 6, if a server error occurs while updating the publication status, the system displays an error message and the group list remains unpublished. EF-02: At any point, if the Lecturer's session expires, the system discards any pending action and redirects the Lecturer to the login page. |  |  |
| **Business Rule** | BR-01: A Lecturer may only publish the group list for classes that have been explicitly assigned to them. BR-02: Once published, all students within the class must be able to view their assigned group immediately. |  |  |

##### **UC22 \- Auto Allocate Students to Groups** 

##### 

| Primary Actor(s): | Lecturer | Secondary Actor(s): |  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Description:** | Allows a lecturer to automatically divide students in a class into groups using the system's built-in algorithm. |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | The Lecturer is authenticated and has an active session. The Lecturer has navigated to the Class Detail page of a specific class. The class has at least two students available for group division. |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | Students in the class are automatically divided into the specified number of groups. The newly generated groups are saved and displayed on the Class Detail page. If the operation fails, no changes are applied to the existing group data. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | NF-01: The Lecturer clicks the Divide Into Group button. NF-02: The system displays a dialog showing the total number of students in the class and an input field for the number of groups. NF-03: The Lecturer enters the desired number of groups → clicks Confirm. NF-04: The system validates the input value →  executes the built-in algorithm to distribute students evenly across the specified number of groups → saves the generated groups → closes the dialog → updates the Class Detail page to display the newly generated group list. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flow:** |  |  |  |
| **Extension Flow:** | ETF-01: At NF-03, the Lecturer clicks Cancel or closes the dialog, the system dismisses the dialog and no division is performed. |  |  |
| **Exceptions Flow:** | EF-01: At NF-04, if the user enters a group number greater than the number of students (the system assigns 2 students from different majors to 1 group), the system displays an error and cancels the submission. |  |  |
| **Business Rule** | BR-01: A Lecturer may only perform group division for classes that have been explicitly assigned to them. BR-02: The number of groups entered must be a positive integer greater than zero. BR-03: The number of groups must not exceed the half total number of students available in the class. |  |  |

| **Business Rule** | BR-01: A Lecturer may only view topic details for groups within their assigned classes. BR-02: A Student or Group Leader may only view the topic details of their own group. ##### **UC25 \- Assign / Change Mentor**

| Primary Actor(s): | Lecturer | Secondary Actor(s): |  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Description:** | Allows a lecturer to assign or change the mentor for a project group. The lecturer can either select an existing mentor from the available list or manually enter the mentor's information if the mentor is not yet registered in the system. |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | The Lecturer is authenticated and has an active session. The Lecturer has navigated to the Topic Detail page or the Group Detail page of a specific group. The selected class and group have been assigned to the Lecturer. The group has a registered topic in the system. |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | The selected mentor is assigned to the group and reflected immediately on both the Topic Detail page and the Group Detail page. If a mentor was previously assigned, the previous mentor is replaced by the newly assigned mentor. If the operation fails, the existing mentor assignment remains unchanged. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | NF-01: The Lecturer selects the option to assign or change the mentor. NF-02: The system displays a dialog or form with two options: select an existing mentor from the available list or manually enter mentor information. NF-03: The Lecturer selects an existing mentor from the available mentor list → confirms the selection. NF-04: The system validates the selected mentor → saves the mentor assignment → displays a success notification and updates the mentor information on the Topic Detail page and Group Detail page. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flow:** |  |  |  |
| **Extension Flow:** | ETF-01: At NF-03, if the Lecturer decides not to proceed, the Lecturer cancels the dialog and the system discards all input without making any changes. ETF-02: At NF-03, if the desired mentor is not yet registered in the system, the Lecturer switches to the manual entry option and enters the mentor's information including name, email, and relevant details → the Lecturer submits the manually entered mentor information → The system creates a new mentor account or record based on the entered information and assigns it to the group →  displays a success notification and updates the mentor information on both relevant pages.. |  |  |
| **Exceptions Flow:** | EF-01: At NF-03, if the selected mentor has already reached the maximum limit of 5 assigned groups, the system displays a validation message indicating that the mentor has reached their group management capacity and prevents the assignment from proceeding. |  |  |
| **Business Rule** | BR-01: A mentor may be assigned to a maximum of 5 groups at any given time across the system; assignment requests that exceed this limit must be rejected. BR-02: A Lecturer may only assign or change mentors for groups within classes that have been explicitly assigned to them. BR-03: A group may have only one active mentor assigned at any given time. BR-04: Assigning a new mentor to a group that already has an existing mentor will replace the previous mentor assignment. |  |  |

##### **UC26 \-Approve / Reject Group**

| Primary Actor(s): | Lecturer | Secondary Actor(s): |  |
| :---- | ----- | :---- | :---- |
| **Description:** | Allows a lecturer to review a pending group and either approve or reject it with an optional reason. |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | The Lecturer is authenticated and has an active session. The Lecturer has navigated to the Group Detail page of a specific group. The selected group belongs to a class assigned to the Lecturer. The group has a current status of Pending. |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | The group status is updated to Approved or Rejected immediately upon confirmation. The updated status is reflected on the Group Detail page and the Group List. If the operation fails, the group status remains unchanged. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | **Approve Group** NF-01: The system displays the group details along with the Approve and Reject buttons. NF-02: The Lecturer clicks the Approve button. NF-03: The system displays a confirmation dialog with an optional reason input field. NF-04: The Lecturer optionally enters a reason for approval → confirms the action. NF-05: The system updates the group status to Approved → closes the dialog and immediately reflects the updated status on the Group Detail page → displays a success notification confirming the group has been approved. **Reject Group** NF-01: The Lecturer navigates to the Group Detail page of a pending group. NF-02: The system displays the group details along with the Approve and Reject buttons. NF-03: The Lecturer clicks the Reject button. NF-04: The Lecturer optionally enters a reason for rejection → confirms the action. NF-05: The system updates the group status to Rejected → closes the dialog and immediately reflects the updated status on the Group Detail page → displays a success notification confirming the group has been rejected. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flow:** | AF-01: At NF-04, if the Lecturer does not enter a reason, the system proceeds with the confirmation using no reason, as the reason field is optional. |  |  |
| **Extension Flow:** | ETF-01: At NF-02, if the Lecturer cancels the confirmation dialog for either action, the system dismisses the dialog and no status change is performed. |  |  |
| **Exceptions Flow:** | EF-01: the Lecturer's session expires, the system discards any pending action and redirects the Lecturer to the login page. |  |  |
| **Business Rule** | BR-01: A Lecturer may only approve or reject groups within classes that have been explicitly assigned to them. BR-02: The Approve and Reject buttons must only be visible and accessible when the group status is Pending. |  |  |

##### **UC27 \- Approve / Reject Project Topic**

| Primary Actor(s): | Lecturer | Secondary Actor(s): |  |
| :---- | ----- | :---- | :---- |
| **Description:** | Allows the Lecturer to review project topics submitted by groups in their assigned classes. The Lecturer can either approve a topic, making it the official project for the group, or reject it with feedback. |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | The project topic has been submitted by a group and is in the Pending state. The Lecturer is assigned to the class where the group belongs. |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | The topic's status is updated. If approved, the topic becomes the group's "Current Version" project. Group members are notified via email of the decision. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | **Approve Topic** NF-01: The Lecturer navigates to the Topic Detail page of a pending topic. NF-02: The system displays the topic details (Title, Description, Objectives, Logo) along with the Approve and Reject buttons. NF-03: The Lecturer clicks the Approve button. NF-04: The system displays a confirmation dialog with an optional feedback input field. NF-05: The Lecturer optionally enters feedback (e.g., "Good choice, proceed with this") and confirms the action. NF-06: The system updates the topic status to Approved → marks it as the official project for the group → closes the dialog and reflects the updated status on the page → displays a success notification. **Reject Topic** NF-01: The Lecturer navigates to the Topic Detail page of a pending topic. NF-02: The system displays the topic details along with the Approve and Reject buttons. NF-03: The Lecturer clicks the Reject button. NF-04: The system displays a dialog requiring a reason for rejection. NF-05: The Lecturer enters the reason for rejection (e.g., "Scope is too broad for this semester") and confirms the action. NF-06: The system updates the topic status to Rejected → closes the dialog and reflects the updated status on the page → displays a success notification. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flow:** |  |  |  |
| **Extension Flow:** |  |  |  |
| **Exceptions Flow:** | EF-01: Invalid Status Transition: If the topic is already Approved or Rejected, the system displays: "You can only review topics that are currently in a Pending state." EF-02: Unauthorized Access: If a Lecturer attempts to review a topic for a class they do not teach, the system returns a 403 Forbidden error. |  |  |
| **Business Rule** | BR-01: Single Source of Truth: A group can have multiple topic versions in the history, but only one topic can have IsCurrentVersion \= true at any given time. BR-02: Finality of Rejection: Once a topic is Rejected, it cannot be reopened; the group must submit a new request (which will be a new ProjectTopic record). BR-03: Version Control: Approval of a new topic version (e.g., after a change request) automatically archives the previous one. |  |  |

##### **UC28 \- View Student List**

| Primary Actor(s): | Lecturer, Student, Group Leader | Secondary Actor(s): |  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Description:** | Provides a comprehensive list of all students enrolled in a specific class. This list includes all students, regardless of whether they have already joined a project group or not. It serves as the primary roster view for class management and coordination. |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | The user is authenticated and has a valid role. The class exists in the system. |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | The user gains an overview of the total student population within the selected class. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | NF-01: The user opens the Student List from their navigation menu. NF-02: The system displays a table showing every student in the class, including their Full Name, Student Code, and Major. NF-03: The user types a name or a student code into the Search Bar to quickly find a specific person. NF-04: The user chooses a specific Major from the filter menu to see only students from that department. NF-05: The dashboard instantly updates the list to show only the students that match the search or filter settings. NF-06: If there are many students, the user uses the Next/Previous buttons at the bottom to browse through the entire roster. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flow:** |  |  |  |
| **Extension Flow:** |  |  |  |
| **Exceptions Flow:** | EF-01: Empty Class: If the class is newly created and no students have been synced yet, the system displays: "There are currently no students enrolled in this class." EF-02: No Matches: If search criteria return zero results, the system displays: "No students found matching your criteria." |  |  |
| **Business Rule** | BR-01: Auto-Class Loading: Students don't need to pick a class; the system automatically shows their own classmates as soon as they open the page. BR-02: Privacy: Contact details like institutional emails are visible to help classmates and teachers communicate, but other personal information remains private. BR-03: Live Count: A counter at the top of the list shows exactly how many students are currently being displayed. |  |  |

##### **UC30 \- Manage Assignment (View / Create / Update / Delete)**

| Primary Actor(s): | Lecturer | Secondary Actor(s): |  |
| :---- | ----- | :---- | :---- |
| **Description:** | Allows a lecturer to manage assignments within their assigned class. The lecturer can view the list of assignments, create new assignments, update existing assignment details, and delete assignments when necessary. |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | The user is authenticated and has an active session. The user holds the Lecturer role and is verified as the instructor in charge of the current class. |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | View: The assignment list is displayed synchronously between Milestones (sorted by sequence) and other assignments (paginated). Create: A new assignment is saved to the database, and students receive an automated email notification. Update: Assignment information is updated. If the due date is changed while submissions exist. Delete: The selected group is removed from the class. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | **View Assignment List** NF-01: The lecturer selects the "Assignment Management" tab within the Class Details page. NF-02: The system retrieves and displays the assignment list in two sections: Milestones: A list of Checkpoints (EXE101) or Outcomes (EXE201). Other Assignments: A list of other small tasks. **Create Assignment** NF-03: The lecturer selects "Add Checkpoint/Outcome" or "Add Assignment". NF-04: The system displays a form including: Grade Item (for milestones), Title, Description, Due Date, Max Score, and Attachments. NF-05: The lecturer fills indeed information into a create form → clicks "Create Checkpoint/Outcome" to submit the form. NF-07: The system validates the data, saves the assignment, and triggers the Email Service to notify all students in the class. NF-08: The system displays a success notification and redirects back to the latest assignment list. **Update Assignment Information** NF-03 (from NF-02 View Assignment List): The Lecturer selects the edit option. NF-04: The system displays an update form including: Grade Item (for milestones), Title, Description, Due Date, Max Score, and Attachments. NF-05: The lecturer uploads instruction files or reference materials (optional). NF-06: The lecturer clicks "Save". NF-07: The system validates the data, saves the assignment. NF-08: The system displays a success notification and redirects back to the latest assignment list. **Delete Assignment** NF-03 (from NF-02 View Assignment List): The Lecturer selects the delete option. NF-04: The system displays a confirmation dialog asking the Lecturer to confirm the deletion. NF-05: The Lecturer confirms the deletion. NF-06: The system removes the selected assignment → displays a success notification and updates the assignment list page. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flow:** |  |  |  |
| **Extension Flow:** | ETF-01: At the deletion confirmation step, if the lecturer selects "Cancel", the system closes the dialog and no data changes are made. ETF-02: In the Create/Edit form, if the lecturer selects a back icon or "Cancel", the system discards all changes and returns to the assignment list. ETF-03 (Quick Toggle Status): At NF-02, the lecturer clicks the Lock/Unlock icon to quickly toggle the status between Active and Closed without entering the edit page. The system performs an immediate update. ETF-04 (Pagination): At NF-02, in the "Other Assignments" section, the lecturer can use pagination of other assignments tables. |  |  |
| **Exceptions Flow:** | EF-01 (Invalid Dates): If the Due Date is set in the past, the system displays the error: "Due date must be in the future." EF-02 (Graded Block): At NF-07 (Update), if the lecturer attempts to change the Max Score while graded submissions already exist, the system displays: "Cannot change max score because some students have been graded." EF-03 (Milestone Limit): At NF-07 (Create), if the lecturer attempts to create/update duplicate grade items, the system denies the request. |  |  |
| **Business Rule** | BR-01: Only the lecturer in charge of the class or the original creator can manage the assignments. BR-02: The system automatically assigns the type: Checkpoint for EXE101 and Outcome for EXE201. BR-03: All deletion actions must comply with the Soft Delete architecture; physical record deletion from SQL Server is prohibited. BR-04: The Due Date must always be scheduled within the duration of the current semester. |  |  |

##### **UC31 \- Export Grade**

| Primary Actor(s): | Lecturer | Secondary Actor(s): |  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Description:** | A lecturer exports the gradebook of a specific class as an Excel file. The exported file contains student information along with their corresponding grades for each grade item configured in the course. |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | The Lecturer is authenticated and is currently on the assignment management page of their assigned class. The class contains students and at least one defined assignment or grade item. |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | An Excel file (.xlsx) containing the detailed class gradebook is downloaded to the Lecturer's device. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | NF-01: The Lecturer clicks the "Export Grade" button. NF-02: Process Data: The button enters a loading state, displaying "Exporting..." with a spinner icon. The system retrieves the class roster, group memberships, and scores for all Checkpoints, Outcomes. NF-04: Once the data is processed, the system automatically triggers the download of the Excel file. NF-05: The system displays a success toast: "Grade exported successfully." |  |  |
| **Alternative Flow:** |  |  |  |
| **Extension Flow:** |  |  |  |
| **Exceptions Flow:** | EF-01: Export Failure: If an error occurs during data retrieval or file generation, the system displays an error message: "Failed to export grade." and reverts the button to its original state. |  |  |
| **Business Rule** | BR-01: Lecturers are restricted to exporting grades only for classes where they are assigned. BR-02: The Excel sheets and columns are generated dynamically based on the specific Grade Items active for that class. BR-03: Data Integrity: The exported values are synchronized with the scores currently visible in the Assignment Management list at the time of the export request. BR-04: File Naming: The file is named according to the server-side convention (typically GradeReport\_\[ClassCode\]\_\[Date\].xlsx) or defaults to grades\_\[classId\].xlsx. |  |  |

##### **UC32 \- Chatting**

| Primary Actor(s): | Student, Mentor, Lecturer | Secondary Actor(s): |  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Description:** | A user communicates with their project group through a group-based chat. Students and group leaders chat within their own assigned group, while mentors and lecturers can select a specific group to chat with. All messages are scoped to the selected group context. |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | The user is logged in. The user belongs to a project team (as a Student, Lecturer, or Mentor). A stable internet connection is available for the real-time service. |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | Messages and files are delivered instantly to all online members. Conversation history is permanently stored and accessible for future reference. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | NF-01: Open the Conversation: The user clicks the floating chat bubble (blue icon with a message circle) at the bottom-right of the dashboard. A tooltip appears: "Open chat". NF-02: Connect and Review History: The Group Chat window opens. The user sees a green status dot next to the title, confirming they are online and connected to the team. The user scrolls up to read past messages. To see older conversations, the user clicks the "Load more history" button at the top of the message list. NF-03: Send a Text Message: The user clicks the input area (Placeholder: "Type a message..."). The user types their message and either presses Enter or clicks the Send icon. The message is instantly displayed to all other team members currently viewing the chat. NF-04: Share a File or Image: The user clicks the Paperclip icon ("Attach file") and selects a file from their device. The user sees the file name and size (e.g., Plan.pdf (120KB)) appear as a preview. The user clicks Send to upload and share the file with the team. NF-05: Check Team Presence: The user clicks the Users icon in the chat header to see a list of all team members and their avatars. NF-06: Minimize Chat: The user clicks the "X" button in the header or the floating bubble again to hide the window. The tooltip confirms: "Close chat". |  |  |
| **Alternative Flow:** |  |  |  |
| **Extension Flow:** |  |  |  |
| **Exceptions Flow:** | EF-01: Connection Lost: If the real-time service is interrupted, the status dot turns gray and the input box displays "Connecting...", temporarily disabling the ability to send messages. EF-02: File Upload Error: If a file fails to upload due to size or connection issues, the system removes the preview and allows the user to try again. |  |  |
| **Business Rule** | BR-01: Access Control: Users can only join and view chat rooms for the specific project teams they are assigned to. BR-02: New Message Notifications: When the chat window is closed, a red Badge on the floating button displays the count of unread messages (e.g., "12" or "99+"). BR-03: Real-time Delivery: Messages are synchronized across all devices instantly via SignalR; if a user is logged in on multiple devices, all will receive the message simultaneously. BR-04: Message Persistence: All chat messages and file links are stored permanently in the database and will be available upon subsequent logins. |  |  |

##### **UC33 \- Active / Close Assignment**

| Primary Actor(s): | Lecturer | Secondary Actor(s): |  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Description:** | A lecturer activates or closes an assignment within their class. When an assignment is activated, students are allowed to submit their work. When closed, the submission period ends and students can no longer submit. |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | The user is authenticated as a Lecturer. The user is the assigned Lecturer for the class containing the assignment. The assignment exists in the system. The lecturer is already on the Assignment Management page. |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | The assignment's status is updated to either "Active" or "Closed". If set to "Closed", students can no longer submit work for this assignment. If set to "Active", students can resume submitting work until the deadline or until it is closed again. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | NF-02: The Lecturer selects a specific assignment. NF-03: The Lecturer clicks the lock icon button. NF-04: The system validates the Lecturer's authority and the current assignment state. NF-05: The system updates the status (swapping "Active" to "Closed" or vice versa) and records the timestamp. NF-06: The system displays a success notification and updates the status indicator on the interface. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flow:** |  |  |  |
| **Extension Flow:** |  |  |  |
| **Exceptions Flow:** | EF-01: Unauthorized Access (NF-04): If a user who is not the assigned Lecturer attempts to change the status, the system returns a "403 Forbidden" error. EF-02: Invalid State (NF-04): If the assignment has been deleted, the system returns a "404 Not Found" error and prevents status changes. |  |  |
| **Business Rule** | BR-01: An assignment must be in "Active" status for the system to accept any new submissions. |  |  |

##### 

##### **UC34 \- Grade Assignment**

| Primary Actor(s): | Lecturer | Secondary Actor(s): |  |
| :---- | ----- | :---- | :---- |
| **Description:** | A lecturer grades submitted assignments by project group. Each group receives a grade for the corresponding assignment based on the lecturer's evaluation. |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | The user is authenticated as a Lecturer. The user is assigned to the class associated with the submission. At least one submission exists for the assignment (in "Submitted" status). |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | The submission status is updated to "Graded". The scores are persisted in the database. Group members receive a notification that their work has been evaluated. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | **Grading a New Submission** NF-01: The Lecturer navigates to the "Assignment Details" page or the "Submissions List" for a specific assignment. NF-02: The Lecturer selects a group's submission to view. NF-03: The Lecturer reviews the submitted files, links, and notes. NF-04: The Lecturer clicks the "Grade" button. NF-05: The Lecturer enters the Score (required) and Feedback (optional) in the grading dialog. NF-06: The Lecturer clicks "Submit Grade". NF-07: The system validates that the score is within the allowed range (0 to Max Score). NF-08: The system updates the submission status to "Graded", saves the evaluation, and triggers a notification to the group. **Updating an Existing Grade** NF-01: The Lecturer views a submission that has already been "Graded". NF-02: The Lecturer clicks the "Update Grade" button. NF-03: The Lecturer modifies the score or feedback. NF-04: The Lecturer clicks "Update Grade" to save the changes. NF-05: The system updates the record and sends a new notification to the group. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flow:** |  |  |  |
| **Extension Flow:** | ETF-01: At NF-03, the Lecturer can switch between different versions of the submission (if the group has submitted multiple times) to see the progression of work. |  |  |
| **Exceptions Flow:** | EF-01: Invalid Score (NF-07): If the entered score exceeds the assignment's Max Score or is less than zero, the system displays a validation error and prevents saving. EF-02: Assignment Deleted (NF-08): If the assignment was removed by an administrator while the Lecturer was grading, the system returns a "404 Not Found" error upon submission. |  |  |
| **Business Rule** | BR-01: Only the Lecturer assigned to the class has the authority to grade its submissions. BR-02: The score must be a numerical value between 0 and the assignment's defined Max Score (supporting one decimal place, e.g., 8.5). BR-03: Once a submission is graded, the group members must be notified automatically through the system's notification service. BR-04: Grading a newer version of a submission automatically marks it as the "Current Grade" for that group and assignment. |  |  |

##### **UC35 \- View Groups In Class**

| Primary Actor(s): | Student | Secondary Actor(s): |  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Description:** | A student views the list of project groups within their enrolled class. This feature is only available after the lecturer has published the group list.  |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | The student is authenticated and enrolled in the class. The group list has been marked as Public by the Lecturer |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | The student successfully views the summary list of project groups. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | NF-01: The student navigates to the Project Groups section within their Class Workspace. NF-02: The system displays a gallery of all groups that have been made public by the Lecturer. NF-03: For each group card, the student can view essential details: Group Identity: The Group Name and the name of the Group Leader. Team Capacity: The current number of members vs. the maximum capacity (e.g., 4/6). Project Topic: The title of the group's chosen or assigned topic (if available). Status: The group's current lifecycle state (e.g., Recruiting, Pending, Approved). NF-04: The student can use the Search Bar to find a group by name or use Filters to sort groups by their current status. NF-05: The system immediately updates the display to show only the groups that match the user's search or filter criteria. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flow:** |  |  |  |
| **Extension Flow:** |  |  |  |
| **Exceptions Flow:** | EF-01: Groups Not Published (NF-02): If the Lecturer hasn't published the groups yet, the system displays: "The group list for this class has not been published yet. Please contact your lecturer for more information." EF-02: No Groups Formed (NF-03): If no groups have been created in the class yet, the system displays: "No groups found in this class." |  |  |
| **Business Rule** | BR-01: Students can only view groups where IsPublic is true. Internal/Draft groups are hidden from general view. BR-02: The "Public" action is a one-way toggle performed by the Lecturer to signal that the group formation phase is finalized. BR-03: Soft-deleted groups are automatically excluded from the list. |  |  |

##### **UC36 \- View Group Details**

| Primary Actor(s): | Student, Mentor, Group Leader, Lecturer  | Secondary Actor(s): |  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Description:** | Actors view the detailed information of a specific project group, including the group's general information, list of members, registered topic, and assigned mentor.  |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | The actor is authenticated. For student actors: The group must be Public OR the student must be a Member of the group being viewed. |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | The actor successfully views the complete profile and status of the group. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | NF-01: Access Group Detail: The actor navigates to a group list (e.g., "Group Management" or "View Groups In Class"). The actor clicks on a Group Name. The system redirects the user to the detail page (Title: \[Group Name\]). NF-02: View General Information: The user reviews the Header card: Group Name: Displays the official team name. Description: Displays the group's intro (Shows "No description" if empty). Status: Displays a badge with the current state (Active, Pending, Rejected, or Draft). NF-03: Review Academic Metadata: The user reviews the info grid: Campus: The branch code (e.g., "HL"). Class: The assigned class code. Semester: The current academic term code. Members: The current total count of students in the team. NF-04: View Project Topic: The user inspects the Topic card: If a topic is registered, the system displays the title and description. If no topic is assigned, the system displays: "No topic assigned yet." NF-05: Inspect Team Roster: The user reviews the Members card: The list shows each member's Avatar (first letter of their name), Full Name, and Student Code. The Leader is identified by a Crown icon and an amber "Leader" badge. Each member's Major Code is displayed for context. NF-06: Return to List: The user clicks the "Back to Groups" button to return to the previous list view. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flow:** |  |  |  |
| **Extension Flow:** |  |  |  |
| **Exceptions Flow:** | EF-01: Access Denied (NF-02): If a student tries to access a non-public group they do not belong to via a direct link, the system returns: "Group is not public or access is restricted." EF-02: Data Sync Error: If mentor or topic information is missing, the system displays: "Information currently unavailable." |  |  |
| **Business Rule** | BR-01: Administrative details (like who removed a member or previous rejection reasons) are restricted to Lecturers, Staff, and the Group Leader. BR-02: Mentors have view access only to the groups they are officially assigned to. BR-03: The detail view always reflects the Current Version of the project topic marked as IsCurrentVersion \= true. BR-04: Student profile information (Email, Phone) shown in the member list follows the system's privacy settings. |  |  |

##### **UC37 \- Register / Change Topic**

| Primary Actor(s): | Group Leader | Secondary Actor(s): | Lecturer |
| :---- | ----- | :---- | :---- |
| **Description:** | Enables a project group leader to formally submit their project topic for approval or request a change to an already approved topic. All submissions are reviewed by the class lecturer to ensure they meet the course objectives.  |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | The student is authenticated and is the Leader of an Approved (Active) project group. The current date is within the allowed periods (Registration Period for new topics, or Change Period for modifications). |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | A topic request record is created with a "Pending" status. The Lecturer is notified (via system dashboard or email) of the new request. Once approved, the new topic becomes the group's "Current Topic". |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | **Viewing Basic Group Info & Roster** NF-01: The actor selects a group from the Class Group List or their personal Dashboard. NF-02: The system validates that the actor has permission to view the details. NF-03: The system retrieves and displays the General Information: Group Name, Description, Status, and Class/Campus affiliation. NF-04: The system displays the Member List, showing: Full Name and Student Code. Major and Campus. Role (Leader or Member). **Viewing Project & Mentorship Details** NF-05: The system displays the Current Project Topic, including: Topic Title and Detailed Description. Project Objectives. Current Approval Status (Pending/Approved/Rejected). NF-06: The system displays Mentor Information (if assigned): Mentor's Full Name and Contact Email. Current Company and Expertise. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flow:** | AF-01: The Leader navigates to a topic previously Rejected by the Lecturer. AF-02: The Leader revises the Title or Description based on the Lecturer's feedback. AF-03: The Leader clicks "Resubmit". AF-04: The system creates a new "Pending" version of the topic, linking it to the group. |  |  |
| **Extension Flow:** |  |  |  |
| **Exceptions Flow:** | EF-01: Not a Leader (NF-02/Scenario 1 & 2): If a regular group member attempts to submit, the system prevents the action and displays: "Only the group leader can perform topic management." EF-02: Registration Deadline Passed (NF-05/Scenario 1): If the deadline has passed, the "Submit" button is disabled, and the system displays the deadline information. EF-03: Change Period Closed (NF-03/Scenario 2): If the TopicChangeEndDate has passed, the system displays: "The period for topic changes has ended." |  |  |
| **Business Rule** | BR-01: Only the Group Leader is authorized to submit, update, or request changes to topics. BR-02: A group can only have one topic in "Pending" or "Approved" status at a time. BR-03: A "Topic Change Request" can only be submitted if the current topic is already "Approved". BR-04: When a new topic (or change) is approved, it automatically supersedes the previous topic as the "Current Version". BR-05: Any rejection by the Lecturer must include feedback to guide the group's revision. |  |  |

##### **UC38 \- Update Topic**

| Primary Actor(s): | Group Leader | Secondary Actor(s): |  |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Description:** | A group leader updates the topic registration or change request while it is still in pending status, before the lecturer has made an approval decision.  |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | The student is authenticated and is the Leader of the group. A topic request exists for the group with a status of "Pending". The topic registration deadline has not yet passed. |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | The project topic record is updated with the new information. The version number of the topic request is incremented. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | NF-01: The Group Leader navigates to the Topic Details page of their submitted proposal. NF-02: The system displays the current topic information and an Edit button (available only for "Pending" topics). NF-03: The Group Leader clicks Edit and updates the Title, Description, Objectives, or Logo URL. NF-04: The Group Leader clicks Save Changes to submit the updated information. NF-05: The system verifies that the topic is still eligible for modification and saves the new details. NF-06: The system updates the topic's version and immediately displays the new information on the page. NF-07: The system displays a success notification: "Updated topic successfully." |  |  |
| **Alternative Flow:** |  |  |  |
| **Extension Flow:** |  |  |  |
| **Exceptions Flow:** | EF-01: Status Changed (NF-05): If the Lecturer approves or rejects the topic while the Leader is editing, the system prevents the update and displays: "Topics can only be updated when their status is Pending." EF-02: Deadline Passed (NF-05): If the topic registration deadline passes before the Leader saves, the system prevents the update and displays: "The deadline for updating the topic has passed." EF-03: Not a Leader (NF-01): If a non-leader member attempts to access the update interface, the system returns a "403 Forbidden" error. |  |  |
| **Business Rule** | BR-01: Updates are strictly limited to topics with a Pending status. Once a topic is Approved or Rejected, it cannot be modified directly (a new request or change request must be used instead). BR-02: Only the Group Leader has permission to update the pending topic. BR-03: Each update increments the VersionNumber to help the Lecturer track that changes have occurred since the initial submission. BR-04: Updating a topic does not reset its "Pending" status; it remains in the Lecturer's queue for review. |  |  |
